rationale: THE DEFECT. page-rerender's check_rerender_mode is ONE conditional with only then/else: five `==` tests on input_data.spec.reason, else_step render_page. render_page re-ships stored HTML and completes green. So an unrecognised routing key is INDISTINGUISHABLE from 'assemble this page' — which is also the estate's safe, cheap, correct default. That is why bugs_open/404 shipped loud-not-refuse and deferred the real repair here: you cannot refuse unknown values of a field whose legitimate values include arbitrary sentences. `[MEASURED 2026-09-02]` spec.reason carried 16 distinct strings across live and archived page_rerender items, four of them free prose (whole sentences, a bug reference, an operator's note), plus routing-SHAPED unknowns that silently assembled: tool_retirement x16, light_palette_chrome_replaced x13, listing_stale x1. WHY THE SPLIT IS WHAT MAKES REFUSAL POSSIBLE. After phases 1a-2, spec.reason is the annotation (free prose, never validated — owner ruling D4, forever) and spec.routing_reason carries only vocabulary values. 'Present but unknown' then has NO legitimate counter-example: verbatim_adoption_deploy (the deliberate assemble-only key) and the migration prose live in spec.reason and stamp nothing. It becomes a mistake BY CONSTRUCTION, and refusable for the first time. WHAT THIS ROUND ADDS, strongest door first. (1) WRITE DOOR (D3): a CHECK constraint on site_work_items scoped to item_type='page_rerender', added NOT VALID. The census showed raw-SQL migration INSERTs are the dominant unguarded producer and no Go code can see them; a bad key now fails the INSERT at the author's desk, synchronously. Unrepresentable beats detectable. (2) READ DOOR: a new START step check_routing_key_known ahead of the gate — absent/empty/known continue, present-but-unknown goes to a refusal step that parks the item at needs_human_review (D1), catching rows that predate the CHECK. (3) check_rerender_mode moves to the TRANSITION clause (every vocabulary value under EITHER key) because narrowing today would route ~1,790 items to assemble — this bug's own shape, fleet-wide, inside its own fix. THE DESIGN PROBLEM THIS SUBMISSION IS ACTUALLY ABOUT is D1's five words 'names the bad key'. fail_work_item's error_message is a config LITERAL, resolved through no path and no template — its read site says so deliberately, so a message cannot be mistaken for a data reference. `[MEASURED 2026-09-03]` 7 live fail_work_item steps across 6 agents configure it and 0 contain '{{'. A static message can therefore name the FIELD (spec.routing_reason) and the vocabulary, but never the key that was actually wrong. Three shapes were considered: (a) a rich static literal — the estate's existing idiom, meta-description-repair's message is this shape, and it keeps the error string CONSTANT so 'how many were refused' stays an equality query; (b) a new dedicated Go action for the refusal — more shared-registry surface than the problem justifies; (c) an opt-in template field on fail_work_item. The owner chose (c). It is the 2026-08-02 §2 shape exactly: the unsafe side is the DEFAULT (absent key = today's behaviour, byte for byte), so the decision is visible to a reviewer of the CALLER, and it does not depend on anyone reading a doc comment. Under RFC_022's three-condition test — opt-in; unsafe side default OFF; zero live consumers, ENUMERATED not asserted — it is not architecture-scope on its own; it is in this round because it ships with the flip that is.

plan.summary: Six in-scope files. (1) Migration 741 (_HOLD, unapplied) inserts two steps and a terminal into the live page-rerender workflow, moves start_step to the new guard, rewrites check_rerender_mode's condition to the transition clause, and adds the write-door CHECK NOT VALID — every string PASTED from livespec renderers, guarded by DO/RAISE before and after, with SET LOCAL lock_timeout. (2) livespec gains two message renderers so the operator-facing message is generated FROM the vocabulary rather than becoming a fourth hand-kept copy of it. (3) fail_work_item gains an opt-in error_message_template with both failure modes loud, plus the ConfigKeys declaration that had to cover all three literals at once, plus a new error code. Proven by executing an apply -> VERIFY -> ROLLBACK round trip against the live database inside a discarded transaction: 741's own verify block passed, the four pasted strings were read back out of agent_definitions and diffed IDENTICAL against the Go renderers, and the rollback restored the pre-flip state (13 steps -> 10, condition byte-exact). Live state re-checked clean afterwards.

edits.symbol: check_routing_key_known, refuse_unknown_routing_key, complete_refused, check_rerender_mode, start_step, chk_page_rerender_routing_reason_vocabulary, snapshot_agent, SET LOCAL lock_timeout
edits.rationale: The flip. _HOLD because owner ruling D2 requires the 404 lane's co-sign and that lane is dormant; the release condition is the co-sign and nothing else. THREE SEPARATE UPDATE STATEMENTS, not nested jsonb_set: nesting jsonb_set(jsonb_set(default_config,'{...,condition}',...),'{workflow,steps}', (default_config #> '{workflow,steps}') || new) reads default_config from the ORIGINAL row for the outer merge and silently DISCARDS the inner condition change. SET LOCAL lock_timeout was added BY THE DRY RUN, not by review: ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID skips the SCAN, not the LOCK, and the same statement measured 2 ms once and >2 MINUTES on an earlier run. A queued ACCESS EXCLUSIVE blocks every subsequent reader and writer of site_work_items behind it, so an unbounded wait stalls the work-item pipeline rather than merely delaying the migration. Failing fast is safe: one transaction, so a timeout rolls back and changes nothing. The pre-guard REFUSES if check_rerender_mode's condition is not byte-exactly the five-value clause this file was generated against — if another lane appended a sixth reason, the pasted transition clause would silently DROP it, which is bugs_open/404's drift committed by the fix for it. Verify is a DO block, not SELECTs: ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty result, so a SELECT-based verify cannot stop the COMMIT.

The refusal message must LIST the legal values (D1). Writing it in the migration would put a FOURTH hand-maintained copy of RerenderSectionReasons into the estate — after the gate condition, the Go reader and the fixer's raw INSERT, which is exactly the drift bugs_open/404 records (two lanes appended a value to this very gate on 2026-08-18 and neither touched Go). Rendered from RerenderSectionReasonNames(), a sixth value reaches the operator's message for free. The '{{...}}' is NOT this package's business to evaluate — it is fail_work_item's opt-in error_message_template, rendered at refusal time. The FALLBACK exists because fail_work_item falls back to the literal rather than failing (parking with a plainer message beats not parking), and an EMPTY fallback would park the item with no explanation at all. Also in this file, and disclosed as a stated blocker in rounds 1a and 1b: CheckRoutingKnownConditionClause now emits `== null` AS WELL AS `== ''`. Discharged by EXECUTING the evaluator — compareValues' nil branch runs BEFORE quote-stripping, so a quoted '' never equals nil and a MISSING key does not match it. The shipped renderer carried only `== ''` and, pasted into 741, would have routed every item minted before phase 2 — the entire legacy population, 1,804 pending items — to human review on flip day.

Renders the opt-in template. BOTH failure modes are loud because a refusal message is read by a human deciding what to do with a parked item, so a message that renders WRONG is worse than one that renders plainly. (1) Option("missingkey=error") makes an absent path an error rather than a shrug. (2) A key that is PRESENT but nil is NOT caught by missingkey — text/template renders '<no value>' — so it is guarded explicitly; a refusal reading routing_reason = '<no value>' would send a reader hunting for a key that is not the problem. This is the trap git_deployer_commit_message_test.go already carries a regression test for ('<no value>' ... that is WHY commit_message_field exists). The error return is the load-bearing part: returning a best-effort string with a nil error would put a half-rendered refusal in front of a human with nothing marking it as degraded.

edits.symbol: FailWorkItemInputSpec, FailWorkItemAction, renderFailWorkItemMessage, failWorkItemTemplateFallbackCode, LogActionEntry, agentType
edits.rationale: Two changes. (a) THE RENDER, opt-in: absent key, nothing runs and the literal stands. __step_error.message still WINS over the template, deliberately — that is today's semantics and a real error from a step that actually failed is better evidence than a message composed in advance; 741's refusal step is reached from a conditional's else branch as the SECOND step of the workflow, so nothing can have failed before it. agentType is HOISTED above the message block because the fallback files an agent_error_log entry and an entry needs the agent type; moving it earlier changes nothing about its value. (b) THE CONFIG DECLARATION, and it is the sharp edge of this edit. checksConfig() is `CheckConfig || len(ConfigKeys) > 0`, so this spec's config detector has been OFF (checked=false) for the whole of the action's life: error_message and status_override are read straight from StepConfig.Config and were declared NOWHERE. Declaring ONLY the new key would have ARMED UnknownConfigKeys against those two and emitted 'Step config carries keys this action does not read - they are silently ignored at execution' about keys the action demonstrably reads, on all 7 live steps. A detector that makes a true statement about the new key and a false one about the old keys is worse than one left off, so all three are declared in one move. StrictConfig stays unset, so an unknown key WARNS rather than rejecting a live workflow — with it set this would have taken six live agents down instead of logging at them. ConfigKeys costs nothing against the RFC_022 optional-key budget: optionalbudget.go excludes it by design, and audit-optional-key-budget.sh reads '0 shared action(s) over it' with this change in the tree. ⚠ For a seat reading this edit alone: renderFailWorkItemMessage is defined in edit 3 of this submission (fail_work_item_message_template.go), failWorkItemTemplateFallbackCode in edit 5 (work_items_common.go), and LogActionEntry is pre-existing in this package — the same helper the bugs_open/396 status_override refusal already files its entry through, which is why the fallback uses it rather than inventing a channel.

Its own agent_error_log code, for the same reason statusOverrideRefusedCode beside it has one: it answers a question no existing code answers — 'the refusal message a human is reading is the FALLBACK, not the intended one'. NOTHING FAILED: the item parked correctly, which is why the severity is warning and not error. Folding it into a generic failure code would bury the one fact that distinguishes it, and a reader querying it wants the misconfigured TEMPLATE, not a failure.

D1 as a test, and the config-detector claim as a DISCONFIRMABLE one. The config test carries a bogus-key NEGATIVE CONTROL: without it, a clean result from a detector that had been switched off again is indistinguishable from a pass, which is the shape this lane's own phase 2b was about. The absent and present-but-nil cases are required to fail through DIFFERENT mechanisms (missingkey=error vs the <no value> guard) so deleting one cannot be masked by the other. specWith ALWAYS sets the key, including for nil: the first draft skipped the assignment when the value was nil, so the present-but-nil test silently exercised the ABSENT case and passed for the wrong reason — the two states are distinct at every layer of this bug, including in the evaluator. MUTATIONS RUN AND OBSERVED FAILING, not asserted: dropping error_message from ConfigKeys gives 'the detector calls [error_message] unknown, but fail_work_item reads them straight from StepConfig.Config'; deleting the <no value> guard gives 'a present-but-nil routing_reason rendered without complaint'. ⚠ The header states these as INSTRUCTIONS, not as 'verified to fail' — the first draft made the claim before running either, which is a checked-looking sentence a reviewer cannot distinguish from a checked one (logged in WRONG_CALLS 2026-09-03, and the reason the imperative form is used here).

plan.risks: (1) THE MIGRATION IS UNAPPLIED AND THAT IS THE POINT. Owner ruling D2 requires the 404 lane's co-sign; that lane is dormant since 2026-08-26. Nothing here is live, so a REVISE costs a file edit and no rollback. (2) THE RESIDUAL I AM NOT CLOSING, stated rather than left implicit: keys_disagree (routing_reason present and DIFFERENT from reason) is 0 today as a property of the PRODUCERS, not of the gate - nothing enforces it. In that state the transition clause routes the item (it matches either key) while rerender_sections is still handed input_data.spec.reason, so shouldStripLiteralMarkdown and the CTA recompute would see the annotation and silently UNDER-DELIVER: this bug's own shape in miniature. Per the lane PLAN those readers move to routing_reason at the NARROWING (phase 3b); the _VERIFY companion counts the state so it cannot arrive unnoticed. I have deliberately NOT invented a lockstep constraint here - that would be re-deciding a ruled design mid-round - but if a seat judges the residual should close in THIS round rather than 3b, that is a fair objection and I will take it. (3) THE NEW BLIND SPOT IS REAL AND ITS REMEDY IS DEFERRED TO THE APPLIER, not to 'later': the five specific livespec edits are enumerated in 741's own header, in the file whoever applies it must open. If a seat thinks a header instruction is too weak a mechanism for this - given that this lane's whole thesis is that prose enforces nothing - that objection lands, and the alternative is to commit the Declarations WITH the apply as one atomic act, which is what the header instructs. (4) The `== null` evaluator fix rides this round without one of its own. It was disclosed as a stated blocker in 1a and 1b and approved both times; it is inert until 741 pastes the clause. Judging it here is correct, and it is flagged rather than buried. (5) __step_error.message still wins over the template. For 741's refusal step nothing can have failed first (second step, reached from a conditional else), but a FUTURE step that is both an error_step target and template-configured would silently get the step error instead. Documented at the read site; not guarded, because changing the precedence would alter behaviour for the seven existing consumers. (6) The CHECK constraint does not cover UPDATEs that predate it, which is exactly why the read door exists as well; and it is added NOT VALID, so history is unscanned until an explicit VALIDATE. The census says that validate would pass with 0 violations today (whole table, all statuses), so the gap is small and measured. (7) text/template over collected_data means an author can name any path in a refusal message, including one carrying site content. The message shipped here names exactly one field. Not gated - a config author can already write arbitrary prose into error_message - but worth a seat's eye if that reads differently.
